questions.question: What is an Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) typically used for, and what distinguishes it from other types of malware?
content: To spread through social media and gain access to personal accounts
To steal sensitive information and sell on the dark web
To disrupt online services and cause financial loss
To infiltrate an organization's network and persist for extended periods

content: It is an example of social engineering
It is a type of virus

It is a type of Trojan horse

content: To increase the speed of data transfer
To secure sensitive information from unauthorized access
To authenticate users' identities
To compress large files

content: Virus
Worm
Trojan
Rootkit

SHA-256 Hashing
bcrypt
PBKDF2 Hashing

content: Weak Password
Compromised Password
Stolen Password
Forgotten Password

questions.question: A company receives an email claiming to be from their CEO, stating that their employee IDs and passwords will be reset due to a recent security breach. The email asks employees to click on a link to update their information.
content: This is an example of a phishing attack
This is an example of a spear phishing attack
This is an example of a whaling attack
This is an example of a pretexting attack

questions.question: What is the primary function of a firewall in network security?
content: To encrypt data transmitted between devices
To authenticate users attempting to access a network
To filter incoming and outgoing network traffic based on predetermined security rules
To provide physical protection for a network device

questions.question: A company's firewall is configured to block all incoming connections by default, but an employee has created a backdoor for a legitimate application. What type of attack is this?
content: Phishing
Denial of Service (DoS)
Man-in-the-Middle (MitM)
Backdoor Attack

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of an anti-beacon or anti-keystroke logger malware technique?
content: To encrypt files and protect against unauthorized access
To monitor system logs for suspicious activity
To prevent a device from being compromised by a malicious beacon signal
To conceal malware payloads within legitimate system software

content: Click on the link and enter your login credentials
Ignore the email and check your bank's official website for updates
Call your bank's customer service number to verify the authenticity of the email
Reply to the email asking for more information

Phishing attacks
Dictionary attacks
Social engineering

content: Denial of Service (DoS) attack
Malware infection
Phishing attack

questions.question: A phishing email is sent to your classmates with a link that promises a free gift card if you click on it and enter your login credentials. However, when you try to open it, it says the sender's email address has been changed.
content: You should ignore the email and not respond.
You should report the email to the school IT department immediately.

questions.question: What is a common mistake people make when creating strong passwords?

Reusing passwords across multiple accounts
Creating passwords that are too long or complex
Changing passwords only every 6 months
